georg-schaeffler.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
georg-schaeffler.period: January 2009 Schaeffler–Continental episode; no current-period evidence reviewed
georg-schaeffler.summary: A 2009 episode reports state-level government discussions of aid for the family-owned Schaeffler group after its Continental takeover. The reviewed pages concern the company and Maria-Elisabeth Schaeffler as owner; they do not show Georg Schaeffler personally negotiating, and no outcome was verified.
georg-schaeffler.mechanism: Corporate financing stress → reported state-aid discussions (outcome not verified)

support.text: Moneycab (26 Jan 2009) reports that Schaeffler had won the Continental power struggle; Handelsblatt reported that Bavaria would back Schaeffler and Lower Saxony Continental, with Seehofer and Wulff reportedly agreeing. Wulff mediated between the companies. Owner Maria-Elisabeth Schaeffler, not Georg, is the family member named.
support.kind: Contemporaneous press report of state-level discussions

support.text: VerkehrsRundschau (26 Jan 2009) reports about EUR 500 million each from Bavaria and Lower Saxony as plans, with form (guarantee, direct stake) open and a condition from Wulff about separating Continental’s core business.
support.kind: Reported plan, not a confirmed decision

counter.text: The Bavarian state chancellery said there were talks but no agreement or commitments; Lower Saxony’s Wulff said no concept was concrete enough. The article labels the reports as unconfirmed.
The reviewed article states the aid was reported plans from newspaper and company sources, not confirmed decisions. No source read establishes final terms, or any personal role of Georg Schaeffler.

georg-schaeffler.limitations: Georg Schaeffler is a family co-owner; the reviewed pages name Maria-Elisabeth Schaeffler. No assessment of donations, later lobbying or the final 2009 aid outcome was possible. A request for crisis aid by a large employer is not itself preferential treatment. Searches were limited and several relevant outlets could not be retrieved; absence of findings here is not exoneration, and donations, lobbying, regulation and newer developments need further research.

michael-hartono.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
michael-hartono.summary: Michael Bambang Hartono died on 19 March 2026, after the wealth date used here. Reviewed sources describe industry-wide tobacco lobbying in Indonesia in which Djarum is named only as a consulted company, and a 2002 BCA acquisition; none establish a personal political exchange.
michael-hartono.mechanism: Industry consultation and past privatization context; personal mechanism not established

support.text: Wikipedia notes the Hartono brothers’ vehicle took 51.15% of Bank Central Asia in 2002, defeating other bidders despite a lower offer, and that BCA shares moved to a holding company during a 2016 tax amnesty. It describes no political ties.

The Jakarta Post (2016) reports that the then industry minister consulted Djarum and Gudang Garam on a tobacco road map and that a minister opened a Djarum sports event; critics cited these as industry interference. It does not allege wrongdoing by Hartono personally.
support.source: The Jakarta Post: pro-tobacco lobby intensifies

counter.text: Fortune’s obituary records his death on 19 March 2026 and mentions an honor at the presidential palace for the 2018 Asian Games; it describes no political bargain or preferential treatment.

michael-hartono.limitations: The family entry shares wealth with brother Robert Budi Hartono; evidence here is not transferred between them. The 2002 bank-sale context is not an allegation and its terms are not analyzed. Indonesian-language sources, Indonesian tobacco excise decisions and donations were not reviewed. Searches were limited and several relevant outlets could not be retrieved; absence of findings here is not exoneration, and donations, lobbying, regulation and newer developments need further research.

nik-storonsky.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
nik-storonsky.summary: Reviewed sources concern regulatory scrutiny of Revolut and reported Russian-link allegations (his father’s Gazprom institute role, an investor’s funding sources). They show friction with, not favor from, UK regulators; no political-power exchange was found. Narrow review.
nik-storonsky.mechanism: None established; reported regulatory friction and unproven link allegations

support.text: Newstream (1 Dec 2025) reports Revolut still lacked a full UK banking licence more than a year after applying, regulators reportedly worried about risk controls, and UK officials reportedly learned of his UAE residence change from the Financial Times. This reflects scrutiny, not preferential treatment.

LRT (22 Jan 2019) reported that his father is a deputy director at Gazprom’s Promgaz research centre, and that Lithuanian MP Stasys Jakeliūnas had requested intelligence reports; the agencies declined to comment. Revolut later confirmed the father’s role.

counter.text: Realtid (4 Mar 2022) reports Revolut says DST Global is a passive minority holder, that the father is an engineer at a research institute, and that Revolut is British and approved by many authorities. The article notes Storonsky renounced Russian citizenship in 2022 per other reports.
counter.kind: Company response and limits of the claims

counter.text: LRT states Revolut said it has no servers or services in Russia. A family member’s employment is not evidence of personal political leverage.

nik-storonsky.limitations: Allegations about a family member and investors are not findings about Storonsky’s own conduct. UK political donations and lobbying were not located in the sources read. Not an investigation. Searches were limited and several relevant outlets could not be retrieved; absence of findings here is not exoneration, and donations, lobbying, regulation and newer developments need further research.

They do not establish a specific preferential exchange.
eric-li.mechanism: Formal consultative roles and company expansion; benefit and exchange not established

support.kind: Roles and press question; secondary source

eric-li.limitations: Claims of provincial-government or bank financing for the 2010 Volvo purchase appeared in search snippets but the pages could not be read, so they are not used. Subsidies, procurement lists and licensing were not analyzed. Political appointments are not misconduct. Searches were limited and several relevant outlets could not be retrieved; absence of findings here is not exoneration, and donations, lobbying, regulation and newer developments need further research.

Charged is not convicted; no wrongdoing is established.
torstein-hagen.mechanism: Alleged hospitality-for-favor in a port matter; case dropped

support.text: Store norske leksikon says Hagen, Bergen mayor Trude Drevland and harbour chief Inge Tangerås were suspected and charged with gross corruption over the 17 May 2015 christening of the Viking Star; Drevland resigned as mayor.
support.kind: Reference summary of a legal episode
